author: /root/capacity_workflow_evidence
role: auxiliary finite source and actual capacity observation; not formal final quality

findings.confidence: confirmed full-materialization behavior; capacity impact requires workload evidence
findings.trigger: GET /api/v1/workflow/tasks/todo or done, page1,size5, while the principal has N matching tasks; pending/open-candidate backlog or accumulated completed history can grow independently of page size.
findings.expectedEngineeringProperty: Evaluate whether a small page should bound task entity materialization; no customer budget/SLA or arbitrary cap is assumed.
findings.actual: At matching N100/1000/10000 each queue returns5 but loads100/1000/10000 WorkflowTask entities. Exactly1 prepared statement and1 native ORM query in all six cases; captured SQL has no database pagination.
counterEvidence: No N+1 in this measured slice: query count remains1 at all scales.
Current controller guards page/size with long bounded arithmetic; no reproduction of old overflow defect.
DHR/foreign higher-rank rows excluded, spoofed assignee ignored, candidate/unrestricted todo membership preserved, order and no-write fingerprints pass.
Baseline source already defines assignee, instance and status indexes; do not invent missing-index diagnosis.
Final growth fixture respects active(instance,node) uniqueness; two earlier incomplete fixture runs are retained and explicitly superseded, not used as final valid-capacity evidence.

growthModel.done: Accumulated completed/rejected/transferred tasks per assignee can grow with operating time; no retention policy was certified.
growthModel.todo: Outstanding and unrestricted/candidate tasks can grow with backlog and broad candidate scopes; not asserted to reach these counts in the actual customer.
growthModel.cost: Database transfer plus ORM materialization grows with all N matches despite fixed returned page P. Full JSONB snapshot/TEXT opinion fields are selected.

optionsForDiscussion.option: Push existing pagination into the same repository query, preserving List/array response and avoiding an unnecessary count query.
optionsForDiscussion.benefit: Bound returned/materialized task entities to requested page.
risks: Preserve existing principal/candidate/unrestricted and nonDHR selection, status filters, order and null placement.
Keep positive page/size/long distant-page compatibility and current default page1,size50; do not silently set arbitrary maximum size.
Timestamp ties need an explicit deterministic pagination choice and regression evidence; adding an id tie-breaker is a behavioral detail to assess.
Database pagination bounds entity materialization but may still scan/sort many rows; inspect actual production-equivalent PostgreSQL plan/index selectivity before claiming overall performance fixed.

optionsForDiscussion.option: Later evaluate lighter query DTOs and endpoint/index changes only if workload justifies them.
optionsForDiscussion.benefit: Potentially avoid carrying large unused scalar snapshots/opinions or improve scans.
risks: Response compatibility and caller inventory required before DTO/protocol changes.
Existing separate indexes and JSONB OR membership mean new indexes require EXPLAIN on representative synthetic current-schema data; no DDL proposed as approved now.

findings.disposition: Report actual evidence and discuss with user first; no implementation, schema/index change, policy cap or protocol change performed.

limitations: Synthetic JWT/filter/MockMvc and native PG/JPA, not password-login/browser/live backend end-to-end.

Probe uses Hibernate create-drop plus the exact active(instance,node) unique partial-index predicate from current baseline; N main tasks have distinct instances and existing workflow references. It does not apply the whole baseline, other production indexes/constraints or migrations; no full current-schema validation.
Numbers prove materialization cardinality in selected requests, not actual peak heap, p95, throughput, OOM or customer capacity. Per-request elapsed nanos are diagnostic only.
Synthetic payloads are small; production JSON/text widths and retention/workload remain unknown.
Only two queues and measured contexts; not a global no-N+1, full workflow or full read/tenant-policy certification.
No server/app deployment, Actions, user database connection, migration or historical restoration.
Owned PostgreSQL left running for root/final QA, not cleaned by auxiliary.
nextAction: Root reviews exact evidence, registers pending-discussion risk and final independent QA can reproduce unchanged eight scenarios on owned PG.
